title: DeckTalk project file
description: Every table of a DeckTalk project file. A document table says what the film is and a tuning table says how it is made, and each key publishes the range that is safe to turn it through.

video.description: These keys set the frame size and the encoding of every recording and of the final mp4.

width.description: Frame width in pixels, for every recording and the final mp4.

height.description: Frame height in pixels, for every recording and the final mp4.

fps.description: Frame rate of the final mp4. The recorder's own rate is measured and is not a setting.
fps.x-hazard: Encoding below the rate the recorder captured at drops presented frames, which both loses motion a viewer saw and corrupts the frames verify measures its own verdicts from.

preset.description: x264 preset. Use veryfast for drafts.
preset.x-range: must be one of ultrafast, superfast, veryfast, faster, fast, medium, slow, slower, veryslow

crf.description: x264 quality. A lower value gives higher quality and a larger file.
crf.x-hazard: Above about 32 the encoder's own ringing is larger than a small reveal, so a cue that played reads as no change and the check that would have caught it passes instead.

slate_color.description: Color of the plain frame that plays when a slate image cannot be rendered, as #RRGGBB or 0xRRGGBB.
slate_color.x-hazard: The colour is placed inside an ffmpeg filter graph and the slate page's stylesheet, so any other text could add a filter that opens a file or a rule that loads a URL.

narration.description: These keys govern how the script is turned into audio.

concurrency.description: How many sections `narrate` voices at once.
concurrency.x-hazard: A voice provider limits requests per account, and a busy answer is retried rather than paid twice.

retries.description: How many more times `narrate` asks again when the voice provider answers that it is busy or failed.

mp3_bitrate.description: Bitrate of the mp3 files that DeckTalk writes, which are the placeholders and the joined narration.

words_per_minute.description: Pacing of the estimated length in the narrate table.

placeholder_words_per_minute.description: Pacing of a placeholder, the click audio a section plays until its take is voiced.

lead_seconds.description: Silence before the first word of every spoken section, so the picture changes before the voice speaks. A section's own `lead_seconds` replaces it.

placeholder_beat_seconds.description: Seconds each beat adds to the length of a placeholder take.

tail_seconds.description: Silence after the last word of every spoken section, so a cut never falls on speech. The take is placed so that exactly this much follows its last sound. A section's own `tail_seconds` replaces it.

takes_dir.description: Directory inside the project that holds every take the film plays and the words its voice sent with each, which you commit so a fresh clone builds the film with no key. The take index stays under the build, because it is a cache built again from the takes. A take is looked for here first and in the machine's take store, `store_dir`, second, and a take this project buys or finds there is written here.
takes_dir.x-hazard: An empty value, a directory outside the project, an absolute path, the project directory itself, a directory inside the build directory or one that holds it is refused when the project loads, because a voiced take must land in a folder the project keeps, and a project someone else wrote would otherwise choose where this machine reads and writes its takes.

store_dir.description: The take store: a folder outside every project where this machine keeps a second copy of every take it buys and the words its voice sent with it, each named by its input digest. A take is looked for here after `takes_dir`, and one found here is checked and copied into `takes_dir`, so a deck with the same words as another plays it without buying it, and a take nobody committed yet survives a `git clean`. Each take is written here once, and a store that already holds a good copy keeps it. It is empty for the `takes` folder in the per-user data folder, such as `~/Library/Application Support/decktalk/takes` on macOS.
store_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type
store_dir.x-hazard: It holds the spoken words of every script voiced on this machine, so keep it out of a synced or shared folder. A relative path, a folder inside the project or one inside the tool cache is refused when the project loads. Write an absolute path or one that starts with ~.

context_characters.description: Characters of each neighbour section sent with a request, for continuous prosody.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before a speech request times out. It is also the longest a run waits while another project on this machine buys the same take, before it is refused as locked.

sound_end_noise_dbfs.description: Level under which the tail of a take counts as silence, which is where the take's sound ends.
sound_end_noise_dbfs.x-hazard: Above about -25 dBFS the scan calls quiet speech silence, so the take is placed early and the cut that follows it lands on a word.

sound_end_min_run_seconds.description: Shortest run under the noise level that counts as the end of a take's sound.

record.description: These keys tune the headless Chromium recording and how narration t=0 is found in it.

settle_seconds.description: Shortest wait after the page is ready and before narration t=0.

cover_min_seconds.description: Shortest time from the start of the recorder to narration t=0.

color_scheme.description: Color scheme that Chromium reports to the page.
color_scheme.x-range: must be one of light, dark, no-preference

page_policy.description: How far `record`, `check` and `storyboard` trust a page. `trusted` lets a page reach the network as a browser would. `untrusted` turns the Chromium sandbox on and refuses every request that is not for the project's own origin, through every channel a page can open. It is the machine's to set, so a project someone else wrote cannot trust its own page.
page_policy.x-range: must be one of trusted, untrusted
page_policy.x-hazard: A service that renders pages other people wrote sets `untrusted` on its machine, because a trusted page can reach anything the machine can, including a cloud metadata endpoint.

concurrency.description: How many page sections `record` records at once. Zero chooses from the CPU this process may use, which inside a container is its quota rather than the host's core count.
concurrency.x-hazard: Each recording needs about two dedicated CPUs to present its frames on time, and a starved recording stalls or lands its reveals late, so a number above the machine's share costs correctness rather than only speed.

retries.description: How many more times `record` records a section whose frames stalled.

cover_scan_seconds.description: Seconds at the start of each recording that `record` scans for the magenta cover.

fallback_first_paint_seconds.description: Guessed first paint when `record` finds no cover and no painted frame. `record` adds `settle_seconds` to it.

cover_min_luma.description: A cover frame has an average luma above this.

cover_max_luma.description: A cover frame has an average luma below this.

cover_min_chroma.description: A cover frame has an average U and an average V above this.

painted_peak_min_luma.description: A painted frame has a brightest luma above this.

painted_mean_max_luma.description: A painted frame has an average luma below this, so a white flash does not count as the picture.

truncated_slack_seconds.description: Allowed shortfall of a recording against its requested length.

frame_gap_max_ms.description: Longest gap between two presented frames after narration t=0. A longer gap makes `record` try again.
frame_gap_max_ms.x-hazard: The runtime reports a gap no finer than its own reporting floor, so a limit under that floor makes every section stall and every retry spend the recording again.

audio.description: These keys are the final audio: its encoding, and the loudness it is normalised to and judged against.

bitrate.description: AAC bitrate of the final mp4.

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate of the final mp4. Every audio input is resampled to it once.

channels.description: Audio channels of the final mp4.

target_lufs.description: Programme loudness the final mp4 is normalised to.

true_peak_max_dbtp.description: Highest true peak the normalised mix may reach.
true_peak_max_dbtp.x-hazard: Four times oversampling under-reads a true peak and the AAC encode overshoots on top of that, so a ceiling above about -1 dBTP reports a clean mix that clips on a listener's decoder.

range_max_lu.description: The loudness range the measurement is made against. It is not a limit, and no mix fails on it.

verify.description: These keys are the limits `verify` judges the assembled mp4 against.

after_dip_seconds.description: Seconds after a section start to the frame that the start check reads.

reference_lead_extra_ms.description: Extra lead added to the reference frame beyond the one the offset limit implies.
reference_lead_extra_ms.x-hazard: The lead is already the offset limit plus the grid guard, so extra lead is only ever the escape hatch for a deck whose reference frame is still inside its own reveal. Above about 80 milliseconds the reference frame reaches back into the previous cue and the check compares two changes rather than one.

probe_delays_seconds.description: Seconds after the cue time for each probe. The later probe catches a slow reveal.
probe_delays_seconds.x-range: must hold at least 1 and must hold values that each must be above 0 and must be at most 10

probe_diff_luma.description: Luma difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed, for the probes and the control shares.
probe_diff_luma.x-hazard: A high value counts only a change that crosses most of the range, so a reveal that fades in or moves a light element on a light slide reads as no change at all.

changed_share_min_percent.description: Smallest share of the frame, in percent, that the reported probe must find changed.
changed_share_min_percent.x-hazard: Above about 5 percent only a change across most of the slide passes, so every small reveal in the deck reports a failure it cannot fix.

margin_min_points.description: Smallest margin, in percentage points, between the reported probe and its control.

thin_change_factor.description: A passing cue whose changed share or margin is under this many times its floor is a warning rather than clean. A value of 1 turns that second opinion off.

onset_rise_points.description: Rise in the changed share from one frame to the next that marks the onset, in percentage points.
onset_rise_points.x-hazard: The rise is measured over a quarter-size frame, so one point is already tens of thousands of pixels. Above about one point no frame ever qualifies, every cue reports a null offset, and the check that names a late reveal stops running while the run still exits clean.

onset_diff_luma.description: Luma difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed, for the onset scan alone.

click_search_seconds.description: Seconds on each side of the cued word's start that the click search covers.

click_floor_dbfs.description: Level a sample must exceed for the click search to call it the click.
click_floor_dbfs.x-hazard: DeckTalk generates its own click at -24 dBFS, so a floor at or above that level finds no click at all and every a/v row measures nothing while reporting no failure.

cue_offset_max_ms.description: How far the measured onset may sit from the cue time, early or late.
cue_offset_max_ms.x-hazard: A viewer sees a reveal land late at about a fifth of a second, so above roughly 200 milliseconds the limit passes films whose pictures visibly miss their words.

av_offset_max_ms.description: How far the click may sit from the word it marks, early or late. It is wider than the cue limit because the click carries the encoder's own jitter as well.
av_offset_max_ms.x-hazard: An mp3 frame smears a transient across about 26 milliseconds and the encode adds its own, so a limit under 80 milliseconds reports a failure that no edit to the film can clear.

black_max_luma.description: A frame whose brightest luma is at most this is black, whether `record` or `verify` reads it.

cut_window_seconds.description: Seconds of narration before each cut that the cut check measures.

cut_max_dbfs.description: Loudest level the cut window may reach before the cut counts as falling on speech.

cut_change_max_percent.description: Largest share of the frame, in percent, that may change across a cut into a seamless section.

voice.description: These keys are the three every voice has: which provider reads the script, in which voice and at what pace. Everything a provider is particular about, its own fields, its model and its rate, is in that provider's own table, so changing `provider` never sends one vendor's fields or model to another.

provider.description: The speech provider that reads the script, which is a name the machine's own map answers. An unregistered name fails when `narrate` runs rather than at load. DeckTalk ships `elevenlabs`, the cloud voice whose own keys are `[elevenlabs]`, and `dtsp`, a voice served by a local server, whose own keys are `[dtsp]`.
provider.x-range: takes any value of its type

id.description: The voice that reads the script, as the provider names it. It is a published name rather than a credential, so it is committed with the project, and it is one of the inputs every take is named by. `DECKTALK_VOICE_ID` overrides it for anyone who keeps it out of the file.
id.x-hazard: The id is placed in the path of every speech request, so a value that could hold a slash, a dot or a query would let a project somebody else wrote send the key to another endpoint of the service.

speed.description: How fast the voice speaks, as a multiple of its natural pace.
speed.x-hazard: The provider refuses a multiple outside its own range, so a slower read is a script change rather than a setting.

mix.description: The settings half of `[mix]`, which is how each layer is ramped. Its files and levels are project content.

duck_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp of the music duck at each edge of a spoken span or a clip.

ambience_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp of the ambience bed at each edge of its span.

ambience_pad_seconds.description: Seconds that the ambience bed extends past each edge of its section.

marker_mute_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp into and out of a marker's mute.

marker_boost_ramp_seconds.description: Ramp into and out of a marker's swell.

motion.description: These keys decide how much motion a build renders, which changes the film it produces.

reduce.description: Render every slide as the reduced-motion variant, which is the film a viewer who asks for less motion should be given.
reduce.x-range: takes any value of its type

scale.description: Multiplier on every declared motion span and duration in the deck.
scale.x-hazard: A scale above one slows motion down, and a span slowed past the measurable ceiling makes its own cue unmeasurable, so each scaled span is clamped at that ceiling rather than obeyed.

elevenlabs.description: These keys are ElevenLabs's own: its speech fields, its model, its rate, its output format and its API. The key it is bought with is `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `base_url` is the machine's to set. The score stage buys from the same API with the same key.

model.description: The ElevenLabs model that reads the script when `[voice] provider` is `elevenlabs`.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

stability.description: How closely the voice holds one delivery across takes.
stability.x-hazard: ElevenLabs takes a share and refuses anything else, so a value read as a percentage fails the request rather than the load.

similarity_boost.description: How closely the voice holds to the original recording it was cloned from.

style.description: How much expressive style the voice adds beyond the words.

speaker_boost.description: Whether ElevenLabs applies its own speaker boost to the take.
speaker_boost.x-range: takes any value of its type

dollars_per_1000_characters.description: What this project's ElevenLabs plan charges in US dollars per thousand characters of speech.
dollars_per_1000_characters.x-evidence: the plan page of the account whose key this project uses
dollars_per_1000_characters.x-hazard: It is zero until somebody states it, and a spend cap refuses a run while the price is still the default, because DeckTalk would otherwise be capping a spend against a number it invented. ElevenLabs bills per character, so a zero somebody stated still asks before it buys.

output_format.description: Audio format ElevenLabs returns each take in, as its own codec_rate_bitrate token. It is part of every take's digest, and its codec names the take's file.
output_format.x-hazard: Every take already bought was bought in the format named here, so another one buys every take again.

base_url.description: Base URL of the ElevenLabs API, which the voice and the score both send their requests and the key to.
base_url.x-range: takes any value of its type
base_url.x-hazard: The script, and for a paid voice the key, travels to whatever host this names, so only the machine names it and a project file that sets it is refused.

dtsp.description: These keys are the `dtsp` voice's own: where its local server listens and the model it reads with. `dtsp` speaks the DeckTalk speech protocol to `decktalk-voice`, a separate local server that is not part of this repository. It needs no key, bills nothing, and `base_url` is the machine's to set.

base_url.description: Base URL of the local speech server, which the script is sent to.
base_url.x-range: takes any value of its type
base_url.x-hazard: The script, and for a paid voice the key, travels to whatever host this names, so only the machine names it and a project file that sets it is refused.

model.description: The model the local server reads the script with when `[voice] provider` is `dtsp`, as the server names it.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

score.description: The settings half of `[score]`: how the music, the ambience and the effects are asked for. Each item's own table holds its prompt and its file, which are project content, beside the settings that size its request, so a key is spelled the same way the item it sizes spells it.

dir.description: Directory inside the project that holds every sound the score bought and the ledger that records them, each named by its item, which you commit so a fresh clone mixes the film with no key. Music bought in parts keeps its parts here, and the piece joined from them is a cache under the build.
dir.x-hazard: An empty value, a directory outside the project, an absolute path, the project directory itself, a directory inside the build directory or one that holds it is refused when the project loads, because a bought sound must land in a folder the project keeps, and a project someone else wrote would otherwise choose where this machine writes what it buys.

provider.description: The sound provider the music, the ambience and the effects are bought from, which is a name the machine's own sound table answers. ElevenLabs is the only sound provider DeckTalk ships, and it buys with the key and `base_url` of `[elevenlabs]`.
provider.x-range: takes any value of its type

output_format.description: Audio format the music, the ambience and the effects are asked for in. A take's format is its voice's own, such as `[elevenlabs] output_format`.
output_format.x-range: takes any value of its type

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before a sound or music request times out.

ambience.description: The settings half of `[score.ambience]`: how the bed is asked for. Its prompt and file are content.

model.description: Model the ambience bed is asked for from.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

duration_seconds.description: Length of the ambience bed that is asked for, which `[mix]` loops under its sections.

prompt_influence.description: How closely the ambience bed follows its prompt.

dollars_per_minute.description: What this project's sound plan charges in US dollars per minute of ambience audio, which is priced by the second of audio asked for.
dollars_per_minute.x-unit: US dollars per minute of audio
dollars_per_minute.x-evidence: the plan page of the account whose key buys the sound
dollars_per_minute.x-hazard: It is zero until somebody states it, and a spend cap refuses a score while any rate it buys at is still the default, because DeckTalk would otherwise be capping a spend against a number it invented.

effects.description: The settings half of `[score.effects]`: how each effect is asked for unless its own table says.

model.description: Model every effect is asked for from, unless its own table names one.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

duration_seconds.description: Length of every effect that is asked for, unless its own table sets one.

prompt_influence.description: How closely every effect follows its prompt, unless its own table sets how closely.

dollars_per_minute.description: What this project's sound plan charges in US dollars per minute of effect audio, which is priced by the second of audio asked for.
dollars_per_minute.x-unit: US dollars per minute of audio
dollars_per_minute.x-evidence: the plan page of the account whose key buys the sound
dollars_per_minute.x-hazard: It is zero until somebody states it, and a spend cap refuses a score while any rate it buys at is still the default, because DeckTalk would otherwise be capping a spend against a number it invented.

music.description: The settings half of `[score.music]`: how the bed is asked for and joined. Its prompt is content.

model.description: Model the music is asked for from.
model.x-range: takes any value of its type

duration_seconds.description: Length of the music that is asked for, which `[mix]` fades out at the end of the film.

bitrate.description: Bitrate of the music file that `score` joins from its chunks.

chunk_max_seconds.description: Longest music request. Longer music is requested in chunks and crossfaded.

dollars_per_minute.description: What this project's sound plan charges in US dollars per minute of music audio, which is priced by the second of audio asked for.
dollars_per_minute.x-unit: US dollars per minute of audio
dollars_per_minute.x-evidence: the plan page of the account whose key buys the sound
dollars_per_minute.x-hazard: It is zero until somebody states it, and a spend cap refuses a score while any rate it buys at is still the default, because DeckTalk would otherwise be capping a spend against a number it invented.

output.description: These keys switch the files a build writes beside the final mp4.

timestamped_copy.description: Write a second copy of the final mp4 named with the date and time.
timestamped_copy.x-range: takes any value of its type

events.description: These keys bound the events files a run writes under `build/events/`.

keep_runs.description: How many runs of event files `build/events/` keeps before the oldest is deleted.

max_bytes.description: Bytes one run's events file may reach before debug and info lines are left out of it. Lines about the run, its stages, its sections, its findings and its costs are always kept.
max_bytes.x-hazard: A file with no bound grows with every tool call a long film makes, on a disk a host shares.

tools.description: These keys name the tools DeckTalk drives, for a machine that supplies its own.

chromium.description: Chromium executable that `record`, `check` and `storyboard` drive. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself, and a path here is what a managed machine sets: a named executable that will not launch is never a reason to download another.
chromium.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffmpeg.description: ffmpeg executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffmpeg.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffprobe.description: ffprobe executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffprobe.x-range: takes any value of its type

timeout_seconds.description: Longest one ffmpeg or ffprobe call, or one wait on another fetch of ffmpeg, may run before it is stopped.

cache_dir.description: Directory the fetched Chromium and ffmpeg builds live in, Chromium in its ms-playwright folder. It is empty for the standard per-user cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type
cache_dir.x-hazard: A relative path is refused when the machine loads. Write an absolute path or one that starts with ~.

project.description: The film itself: its name, its deck and the files it is built from.

section.description: One section of the script, in the order the film plays them.

items.description: One section of the script, in the order the film plays them.

transition.description: How one section is joined to the next.

x-numbers.description: Derived: every share is measured over the frame scaled down by PROBE_SCALE, at every frame size.
Derived: every share is measured over the frame scaled down by PROBE_SCALE, at every frame size.
Derived: one pixel per H.264 transform block, so the block average cancels the encoder's ringing at every frame size rather than only at 1080p.
Derived: one pixel per H.264 transform block, so the block average cancels the encoder's ringing at every frame size rather than only at 1080p.
Derived: the reference frame has to sit outside the window the offset limit allows, or the check compares a cue against a frame the same cue had already changed.
Truth: the rate the recorder captures at, which DeckTalk cannot set and so never asks for.
Calibration: a frame a quarter the film's size keeps every share a cue can move while comparing a sixteenth of the pixels.
Truth: the H.264 transform block the block-averaged copy of a frame cancels ringing over.
Truth: half a frame of rounding guard on each side of the window the offset limit allows.
Calibration: the runtime's own reporting floor, under which a frame gap cannot be seen.
Truth: the level DeckTalk generates its own click at, which every click floor sits under.
Truth: the span at which an effect covers its own cue, which is the ceiling every declared span, every scaled span and every staggered total is held under.
